recent_commits.message: The OpenScales OSD export now exists end-to-end. Work spanned three files:
recent_commits.body:
R/data_check_helpers.R — two shared, package-level helpers (so both the module and the converter can call them):

.osd_safe_code() — spec-valid code sanitizer.
.osd_code_and_provenance() — the three-tier provenance/code minting (dictionary → bare official code or curated METACHECK-; manuscript → METACHECK-; self-generated → METACHECK-GEN-), each with a human-readable provenance sentence.
inst/modules/codebook_check.R — rewrote .scales_to_osd(scale_groups, columns_df, labels_df, dict):

Spec-conformant structure: osd_version, definition.{scale_info, likert_options, items}, translations.en, plus a namespaced definition.metacheck block for provenance/confidence/source (kept out of the spec objects).
likert_options lets the codebook lead — decodes value_labels for range + anchor labels (source:"codebook"); falls back to observed min/max/n_unique from data_check stats (source:"observed"); omitted entirely when nothing is scale-shaped (no invention).
translations.en carries codebook item wording; text_key points at it per spec.
Named groups flagged write=TRUE; unnamed detections write=FALSE (report-only, no file).
R/psychds-convert.R — the file writer + cross-reference:

.osd_write_scales() writes one scales/{CODE}/{CODE}.osd per named scale (pretty JSON) under the dataset root.
.osd_write_readme_section() appends a "Psychometric scales" section to the root README.md explaining the three provenance markers and listing every scale (your "general README" decision).
Added metacheck:scale code + source to variableMeasured, so Psych-DS variables cross-reference their OSD definition.
n_scales added to the return list and completion message.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): RC-T caption-tail walk — tables no longer drop their first rows (v2.4.119)
recent_commits.body:
The gated RC-T cycle (user-approved). `_extract_table_body_text`'s body_start
walk stepped break-to-break (preferring \n\n) with a 40-char window, so a
WRAPPED caption whose table body serializes column-by-column overshot the
caption's own terminator and SILENTLY DROPPED leading rows — chan_feldman
Table 3 lost its first four rows, Table 1 its first hypothesis row.

`_caption_tail_body_start` replaces it with a per-LINE walk carrying three
structural rules, each pinned by a corpus case the run-3 prototype regressed
on: whole-line terminator test (xiao T6), blank-line stop, and a max-wrap-lines
cap (amc_1 T3). Companion guards handle what the corrected walk now reaches:
`_skip_leading_nontable_junk` (leading figure caption / wrapped prose, bounded
+ terminated-only) and `_raw_text_is_page_furniture_only` (jama_open_1 T2
rendered ONLY a banner/title/date/"8/13"). `_line_is_body_prose` gains a
bibliography-row exemption.

Two corruptions the recovered rows EXPOSED (pre-existing, verified against a
v2.4.118 baseline — the data simply never reached the page before):
- S5b FFFD `>=` recovery was wired into channel 1 only, so plos_med Table 2's
  rows arrived as mojibake. Now wired into channel 3, with the document-
  consensus gate extended to count operators already present (unanimity kept).
- W0b-est: the estimate column is separated from its CI column by the SE
  column, so W0d's proximity window cannot span it (efendic T3 `21.34`).
  Estimates now pair with CIs POSITIONALLY, rewriting only when the corrected
  reading lands inside that CI and the literal one does not.

A recovery REJECTED before release: a `W0b-col` column-consensus rule flipped
efendic T5's `[2.42, 2.69]`, which the AI gold confirms is a GENUINELY POSITIVE
interval (Direction high-vs-low, est 2.56, p<.001) — it would have published a
sign-flipped effect. Removed; the case is pinned by a regression guard. The
pre-existing `_CORRUPT_CI_RE` was itself over-broad (matched ascending pairs,
asserting the wrong flip into existence) and is now descending-only. Standing
rule: a sign flip requires per-record evidence, never column membership.

Free, open-source AI academic paper reviewer that outperforms popular paid AI reviewers.

You provide your own API key and pay the LLM provider directly — typically **under $2 per review**.

Don't want to run it locally? Use the [web interface](https://coarse.ink/) instead.


Get an API key from [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/keys) (free to sign up), then:

```bash
uvx coarse-ink review paper.pdf --api-key sk-or-v1-YOUR_KEY
```

That's it. The review is written to `paper_review.md` in the current directory.


coarse requires Python 3.12+. If you don't have `uvx`, install [uv](https://docs.

recovery that would have published a sign-flipped CI), the fix-as-defect-
detector pattern, and the process misses (git stash in a shared tree; a

highlights.message: fix(tables): RC-T caption-tail walk — tables no longer drop their first rows (v2.4.119)
highlights.body:
The gated RC-T cycle (user-approved). `_extract_table_body_text`'s body_start
walk stepped break-to-break (preferring \n\n) with a 40-char window, so a
WRAPPED caption whose table body serializes column-by-column overshot the
caption's own terminator and SILENTLY DROPPED leading rows — chan_feldman
Table 3 lost its first four rows, Table 1 its first hypothesis row.

`_caption_tail_body_start` replaces it with a per-LINE walk carrying three
structural rules, each pinned by a corpus case the run-3 prototype regressed
on: whole-line terminator test (xiao T6), blank-line stop, and a max-wrap-lines
cap (amc_1 T3). Companion guards handle what the corrected walk now reaches:
`_skip_leading_nontable_junk` (leading figure caption / wrapped prose, bounded
+ terminated-only) and `_raw_text_is_page_furniture_only` (jama_open_1 T2
rendered ONLY a banner/title/date/"8/13"). `_line_is_body_prose` gains a
bibliography-row exemption.

Two corruptions the recovered rows EXPOSED (pre-existing, verified against a
v2.4.118 baseline — the data simply never reached the page before):
- S5b FFFD `>=` recovery was wired into channel 1 only, so plos_med Table 2's
  rows arrived as mojibake. Now wired into channel 3, with the document-
  consensus gate extended to count operators already present (unanimity kept).
- W0b-est: the estimate column is separated from its CI column by the SE
  column, so W0d's proximity window cannot span it (efendic T3 `21.34`).
  Estimates now pair with CIs POSITIONALLY, rewriting only when the corrected
  reading lands inside that CI and the literal one does not.

A recovery REJECTED before release: a `W0b-col` column-consensus rule flipped
efendic T5's `[2.42, 2.69]`, which the AI gold confirms is a GENUINELY POSITIVE
interval (Direction high-vs-low, est 2.56, p<.001) — it would have published a
sign-flipped effect. Removed; the case is pinned by a regression guard. The
pre-existing `_CORRUPT_CI_RE` was itself over-broad (matched ascending pairs,
asserting the wrong flip into existence) and is now descending-only. Standing
rule: a sign flip requires per-record evidence, never column membership.

Also: tests/conftest.py resolved fixtures under the dead ~/Dropbox/Vibe path,
so every articlerepo-keyed test SKIPPED silently (a green run that verified
nothing). Now VIBE_ROOT-aware.

Verification: 101-PDF guard-diff 333 captions recover / 0 truncations (the
prototype had 2); full suite 1872 passed (the one red is a load-sensitive
perf test that passes in isolation at 1.43s of a 5s budget); baseline 26/26;
5-paper canary AI-verify — each fix independently confirmed by an auditor
told to check for it.

highlights.message: release(glyph): W0n p-threshold dropped-decimal recovery — v2.4.118
highlights.body:
ar_apa/JESP rendered `p < 05 (see Fig. 1)` — the significance threshold's
decimal point is drawn on the AdvGulliv broken-ToUnicode family and vanishes
from BOTH text channels (pdftotext emits nothing; the pdfplumber char stream
reads `p<05(see` with no dot char), so unlike W0h/W0m there is no layout
evidence to gate on. W0n `recover_p_threshold_dropped_decimal` is a pure
text-shape recovery: a dotless, leading-zero-free canonical threshold
(05/01/001) after `<`/`>`/`≤`/`≥` is never legitimate notation. Four guards
(never `=`; canonical set only; no longer-number continuation;
significance-clause context) keep the 10-fold-wrong-number FP impossible on
the shapes the corpus actually contains (only other dotless sites corpus-wide
are legitimate `P = 1` exact values, excluded by the operator guard). Wired
channels 1+3; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.45.

adversarial battery; real-PDF test fails at v2.4.117; full suite 1865 passed

confirms `p < .05 (see Fig. 1)` matches gold with healthy thresholds
byte-identical.

highlights.message: release(glyph): W0m β-as-'b' layout-gated recovery — v2.4.117 packaging
highlights.body:
Completes the v2.4.117 release for the W0m code that landed via 3b24a20 (the
Dropbox-damage restore commit recovered the uncommitted routine intact):
version bumps (__version__/pyproject 2.4.117; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.44 was
in the restored file), CHANGELOG entry, tests, project lesson.

W0m recover_beta_via_layout: ar_apa (JESP 2009) drew the Greek β in the AdvPSMP
math-symbol font with no ToUnicode CMap, so pdftotext rendered all five
standardized coefficients as plain 'b' (`b = -.022` for `β = −.022`). A
text-only rewrite is unsafe ('b', unstandardized, is a legitimate distinct
statistic) — the layout font tag is the discriminator: a 'b' char in an
AdvPSMP-family font immediately before '=' is a corrupted β; flips at most as
many text slots as the layout counted (the W0h correlation mechanism).

Verification (ground truth = AI multimodal reading golds via article-finder):
- Independent Sonnet audit: all five ar_apa betas render β (4 signed correct;
  .245's minus stays the documented OCR-only limit). maier rotation audit:
  ZERO b→β false positives; H3a/H3b intact.
- 101-PDF layout FP scan: fires ONLY on the 2 JESP-2009 sibling papers
  (target + _010, 13 more betas recovered by the same font signature).
- Glyph+idempotency suite 97 passed; 26-paper baseline 26/26; 5 new unit tests
  + real-PDF render test asserting β (fails at v2.4.116).
- Also repaired the post-move broken editable install (pip -e at ~/Vibe).
